parts.label: (a)
hints: Use the standard definition of conditional probability: $P(A \mid B) = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)}$.
Substitute the given intersection probability $0.15$ and condition probability $0.60$.

walkthrough.text:
State the conditional probability formula:
$$P(A \mid B) = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)}$$

Substitute the numerical values and evaluate:
$$P(A \mid B) = \frac{0.15}{0.60} = 0.25 = \frac{1}{4}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Apply the definition of conditional probability restricting to event $B$:
$$P(A \mid B) = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)}$$

Substitute given values directly and reduce:
$$P(A \mid B) = \frac{0.15}{0.60} = \frac{1}{4} = 0.25$$

ai_rubric.observable: Apply the conditional probability formula $P(A \mid B) = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)}$ by substituting $\frac{0.15}{0.60}$.

parts.label: (a)
hints: The words 'given that the student plays drums' restrict the sample space to only the drum players.
Place the total number of drum players in the denominator and the male drum players in the numerator.

walkthrough.text:
Restrict the sample space to the condition 'plays drums':
$$\text{Condition denominator} = 30$$

Count the number of male drum players and form the fraction:
$$P(\text{male} \mid \text{drums}) = \frac{12}{30} = \frac{2}{5} = 0.4$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Restrict focus solely to the subset satisfying the given condition:
$$\text{Sample space} = \text{Drum players} = 30$$

Divide the count of male students within that subgroup by the subgroup total:
$$P(\text{male} \mid \text{drums}) = \frac{12}{30} = \frac{2}{5} = 0.4$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identify the restricted sample space of 30 drum players as the denominator and state $\frac{12}{30}$.

parts.label: (a)
hints: List all pairs $(d_1, d_2)$ that contain at least one 2, being careful not to double-count $(2,2)$.
Among these valid pairs, count how many have a sum equal to 6.

walkthrough.text:
List the restricted set of pairs having at least one 2:
$$\text{Restricted set} = \{(2,1), (2,2), (2,3), (2,4), (1,2), (3,2), (4,2)\} \implies 7 \text{ outcomes}$$

Identify pairs whose sum is 6 within this restricted set:
$$\text{Favourable pairs} = \{(2,4), (4,2)\} \implies 2 \text{ outcomes}$$

Calculate the conditional probability:
$$P(\text{sum } 6 \mid \ge 1 \text{ two}) = \frac{2}{7}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Restrict the sample space to outcomes containing at least one 2 without duplication:
$$n(\ge 1 \text{ two}) = 7$$

Select outcomes within this restricted set that sum to 6:
$$\text{Favourable} = \{(2,4), (4,2)\} \implies n(\text{sum } 6 \cap \ge 1 \text{ two}) = 2$$

Form the probability ratio:
$$P(\text{sum } 6 \mid \ge 1 \text{ two}) = \frac{2}{7}$$

ai_rubric.observable: List or count the 7 equally likely outcomes containing at least one 2 without double-counting $(2,2)$ and identify the 2 outcomes with sum 6 ($(2,4)$ and $(4,2)$).

parts.label: (a)
hints: Conditioning on $B'$ means using $P(B')$ as the denominator.
Find $P(B') = 1 - P(B)$ and compute $\frac{P(A \cap B')}{P(B')}$.

walkthrough.text:
Determine the probability of the conditioning event $B'$:
$$P(B') = 1 - P(B) = 1 - 0.40 = 0.60$$

Apply the conditional probability formula with denominator $P(B')$:
$$P(A \mid B') = \frac{P(A \cap B')}{P(B')} = \frac{0.18}{0.60} = 0.30 = \frac{3}{10}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Compute the complement probability for the condition:
$$P(B') = 1 - 0.40 = 0.60$$

Evaluate the conditional probability ratio:
$$P(A \mid B') = \frac{P(A \cap B')}{P(B')} = \frac{0.18}{0.60} = 0.3 = \frac{3}{10}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculate the complement denominator $P(B') = 1 - 0.40 = 0.60$ and substitute into $\frac{P(A \cap B')}{P(B')} = \frac{0.18}{0.60}$.

parts.label: (a)
hints: The first score is odd, so it must be either 1 or 3.
List all 6 possible pairs with first score odd and count those whose product is at most 3.

walkthrough.text:
Determine all outcomes where the first score is odd (1 or 3):
$$\text{Restricted pairs} = \{(1,1), (1,2), (1,3), (3,1), (3,2), (3,3)\} \implies 6 \text{ outcomes}$$

Count pairs with product $\le 3$:
$$\text{Products: } 1\times 1=1, \; 1\times 2=2, \; 1\times 3=3, \; 3\times 1=3 \implies 4 \text{ pairs}$$

Calculate the conditional probability:
$$P(\text{product} \le 3 \mid \text{first odd}) = \frac{4}{6} = \frac{2}{3}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Identify the size of the restricted sample space:
$$n(\text{first odd}) = 2 \times 3 = 6$$

Filter by the product condition $\le 3$:
$$\text{Valid} = \{(1,1), (1,2), (1,3), (3,1)\} \implies n(\text{valid}) = 4$$

Compute and reduce the ratio:
$$P = \frac{4}{6} = \frac{2}{3}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Restrict sample space to the 6 pairs where the first score is odd and identify the 4 pairs with product $\le 3$ ($(1,1), (1,2), (1,3), (3,1)$).

parts.label: (a)
hints: Recall the definition $P(A \mid B) = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)}$.
Divide $0.45$ by $0.75$ and simplify.

walkthrough.text:
Set up the conditional probability quotient:
$$P(A \mid B) = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)} = \frac{0.45}{0.75}$$

Simplify the decimal quotient:
$$P(A \mid B) = \frac{45}{75} = \frac{3}{5} = 0.60$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Apply the standard ratio definition for conditional probability:
$$P(A \mid B) = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)}$$

Substitute given values and reduce to simplest fraction:
$$P(A \mid B) = \frac{0.45}{0.75} = \frac{3}{5} = 0.6$$

ai_rubric.observable: State or substitute values into the conditional probability formula $P(A \mid B) = \frac{0.45}{0.75}$.

parts.label: (a)
hints: The condition 'given that the student is a Senior' restricts the total to the Senior row.
Find the row total for Seniors and place the number of Senior Art students over this total.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the total number of Senior students:
$$\text{Total Seniors} = 10 + 30 + 30 = 70$$

Form the conditional probability using the Senior row:
$$P(\text{Art} \mid \text{Senior}) = \frac{30}{70} = \frac{3}{7}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Restrict analysis exclusively to the Senior row:
$$n(\text{Senior}) = 10 + 30 + 30 = 70$$

Divide the Senior Art count by the total Senior count:
$$P(\text{Art} \mid \text{Senior}) = \frac{30}{70} = \frac{3}{7}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Restrict to the Senior row with total $10 + 30 + 30 = 70$ and form fraction $\frac{30}{70}$.

parts.label: (b)
hints: The condition 'given that the student takes Music' restricts the total to the Music column.
Sum the Music column for the denominator and place the Junior Music students in the numerator.

walkthrough.text:
Find the sum of all students in the Music column:
$$\text{Total Music} = 45 + 30 = 75$$

Compute the conditional probability:
$$P(\text{Junior} \mid \text{Music}) = \frac{45}{75} = \frac{3}{5} = 0.6$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Restrict focus to the Music column total:
$$n(\text{Music}) = 45 + 30 = 75$$

Divide the Junior Music students by the total Music students:
$$P(\text{Junior} \mid \text{Music}) = \frac{45}{75} = \frac{3}{5} = 0.6$$

ai_rubric.observable: Restrict to the Music column with total $45 + 30 = 75$ and form fraction $\frac{45}{75}$.

parts.label: (a)
hints: When the first die is fixed as 3, the sum depends entirely on the second die.
Since 3 is odd, the sum is odd if and only if the second die shows an even number (2, 4, or 6).

walkthrough.text:
List the 6 possible outcomes when the first die is 3:
$$\text{Outcomes} = \{(3,1), (3,2), (3,3), (3,4), (3,5), (3,6)\}$$

Select outcomes where the sum is odd:
$$\text{Odd sums} = \{(3,2), (3,4), (3,6)\} \implies 3 \text{ outcomes}$$

Calculate the conditional probability:
$$P(\text{sum odd} \mid d_1 = 3) = \frac{3}{6} = \frac{1}{2} = 0.5$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Define the sample space restricted by $d_1 = 3$:
$$n(d_1 = 3) = 6$$

Count outcomes yielding an odd sum:
$$\text{Favourable} = \{(3,2), (3,4), (3,6)\} \implies n = 3$$

Obtain the conditional probability:
$$P = \frac{3}{6} = \frac{1}{2}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identify the 6 possible outcomes when the first die is 3 ($(3,1)$ to $(3,6)$) and count those with odd sum ($(3,2), (3,4), (3,6)$).

parts.label: (b)
hints: First list all possible pairs on two six-sided dice that sum to 8.
Check which of these pairs have a prime number (2, 3, or 5) on the first die.
Divide the number of prime-first pairs by the total number of pairs summing to 8.

walkthrough.text:
List all pairs of dice outcomes that give a sum of 8:
$$\text{Pairs summing to 8} = \{(2,6), (3,5), (4,4), (5,3), (6,2)\} \implies 5 \text{ pairs}$$

Identify which pairs have a prime first die (prime numbers on a standard die are 2, 3, and 5):
$$\text{Favourable pairs} = \{(2,6), (3,5), (5,3)\} \implies 3 \text{ pairs}$$

Compute the conditional probability:
$$P(d_1 \text{ is prime} \mid \text{sum } 8) = \frac{3}{5} = 0.6$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Identify the restricted subset of outcomes with sum equal to 8:
$$S_{\text{sum}=8} = \{(2,6), (3,5), (4,4), (5,3), (6,2)\} \implies n = 5$$

Select outcomes where the first score is a prime number:
$$\text{Primes in } \{2,3,4,5,6\} = \{2,3,5\} \implies \text{Pairs: } (2,6), (3,5), (5,3)$$

Evaluate the probability ratio:
$$P(d_1 \text{ prime} \mid \text{sum } 8) = \frac{3}{5} = 0.6$$

ai_rubric.observable: List the 5 equally likely pairs that give a sum of 8: $(2,6), (3,5), (4,4), (5,3), (6,2)$.
Identify the outcomes where the first die is prime (2, 3, or 5): $(2,6), (3,5), (5,3)$.

parts.label: (a)
hints: Being late can happen via bus or via train.
Multiply along each mode's late branch and sum: $P(\text{Late}) = P(\text{Bus} \cap \text{Late}) + P(\text{Train} \cap \text{Late})$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate late probabilities for each transport mode:
$$P(\text{Bus} \cap \text{Late}) = 0.60 \times 0.05 = 0.03$$
$$P(\text{Train} \cap \text{Late}) = 0.40 \times 0.15 = 0.06$$

Sum the probabilities of these mutually exclusive paths:
$$P(\text{Late}) = 0.03 + 0.06 = 0.09$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Apply the law of total probability across both transit routes:
$$P(\text{Late}) = P(\text{Bus})P(\text{Late} \mid \text{Bus}) + P(\text{Train})P(\text{Late} \mid \text{Train})$$

Evaluate the path products and sum:
$$P(\text{Late}) = (0.60 \times 0.05) + (0.40 \times 0.15) = 0.03 + 0.06 = 0.09$$

ai_rubric.observable: Apply the law of total probability across bus and train paths: $(0.60 \times 0.05) + (0.40 \times 0.15)$.

parts.label: (b)
hints: Use Bayes' theorem: $P(\text{Train} \mid \text{Late}) = \frac{P(\text{Train} \cap \text{Late})}{P(\text{Late})}$.
The numerator is the train-and-late branch probability $0.40 \times 0.15$.
The denominator is the overall late probability $0.09$ calculated in part (a).

walkthrough.text:
State the conditional probability formula:
$$P(\text{Train} \mid \text{Late}) = \frac{P(\text{Train} \cap \text{Late})}{P(\text{Late})}$$

Substitute values from part (a):
$$P(\text{Train} \cap \text{Late}) = 0.06, \quad P(\text{Late}) = 0.09$$

Simplify the fraction:
$$P(\text{Train} \mid \text{Late}) = \frac{0.06}{0.09} = \frac{6}{9} = \frac{2}{3}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Apply Bayes' theorem to reverse the conditioning:
$$P(\text{Train} \mid \text{Late}) = \frac{P(\text{Train} \cap \text{Late})}{P(\text{Late})}$$

Substitute the specific branch value and the total late probability:
$$P(\text{Train} \mid \text{Late}) = \frac{0.06}{0.09}$$

Reduce to simplest fraction:
$$P(\text{Train} \mid \text{Late}) = \frac{2}{3}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Substitute the numerator $0.40 \times 0.15 = 0.06$ and denominator $0.09$ from part (a).

parts.label: (a)
hints: Notice that 'not late' is the complement of 'late'.
Use the result $P(\text{Late}) = 0.09$ from the previous problem: $P(\text{Not Late}) = 1 - P(\text{Late})$.
Alternatively, sum the on-time paths: $(0.60 \times 0.95) + (0.40 \times 0.85)$.

walkthrough.text:
Recognize that 'not late' is the complement of 'late':
$$P(\text{Not Late}) = 1 - P(\text{Late})$$

Substitute $P(\text{Late}) = 0.09$:
$$P(\text{Not Late}) = 1 - 0.09 = 0.91$$

Verify by calculating on-time branches directly:
$$P(\text{Not Late}) = (0.60 \times 0.95) + (0.40 \times 0.85) = 0.57 + 0.34 = 0.91$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Formulate the complement probability of being on time:
$$P(\text{Not Late}) = 1 - P(\text{Late})$$

Evaluate the difference directly:
$$P(\text{Not Late}) = 1 - 0.09 = 0.91$$

Confirm via the direct branch sum:
$$P(\text{Not Late}) = 0.57 + 0.34 = 0.91 = \frac{91}{100}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identify the complement relationship $P(\text{Not Late}) = 1 - P(\text{Late})$ or set up the direct sum $(0.60 \times 0.95) + (0.40 \times 0.85)$.

parts.label: (b)
hints: Apply Bayes' theorem: $P(\text{Bus} \mid \text{Not Late}) = \frac{P(\text{Bus} \cap \text{Not Late})}{P(\text{Not Late})}$.
Calculate the numerator as $P(\text{Bus}) \times P(\text{Not Late} \mid \text{Bus}) = 0.60 \times 0.95$.
Divide by the denominator $0.91$ found in part (a).

walkthrough.text:
State the conditional probability formula for the event 'not late':
$$P(\text{Bus} \mid \text{Not Late}) = \frac{P(\text{Bus} \cap \text{Not Late})}{P(\text{Not Late})}$$

Calculate the bus-and-not-late numerator:
$$P(\text{Bus} \cap \text{Not Late}) = 0.60 \times 0.95 = 0.57$$

Divide by the denominator $0.91$ from part (a):
$$P(\text{Bus} \mid \text{Not Late}) = \frac{0.57}{0.91} = \frac{57}{91}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Apply Bayes' theorem with the restricted 'not late' condition:
$$P(\text{Bus} \mid \text{Not Late}) = \frac{P(\text{Bus} \cap \text{Not Late})}{P(\text{Not Late})}$$

Insert the calculated branch and total probabilities:
$$P(\text{Bus} \mid \text{Not Late}) = \frac{0.60 \times 0.95}{0.91} = \frac{0.57}{0.91}$$

Convert to simplest exact integer ratio:
$$P(\text{Bus} \mid \text{Not Late}) = \frac{57}{91}$$

ai_rubric.observable: State the conditional probability formula $P(\text{Bus} \mid \text{Not Late}) = \frac{P(\text{Bus} \cap \text{Not Late})}{P(\text{Not Late})}$.
Substitute the numerator $0.60 \times 0.95 = 0.57$ and denominator $0.91$ from part (a).

parts.label: (a)
hints: Defective components come from three mutually exclusive sources: Machine $A$, Machine $B$, or Machine $C$.
Multiply each machine's production proportion by its defect rate.
Sum the three path probabilities: $P(D) = P(A \cap D) + P(B \cap D) + P(C \cap D)$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the defect probability contributed by each machine:
$$P(A \cap D) = 0.50 \times 0.02 = 0.010$$
$$P(B \cap D) = 0.30 \times 0.03 = 0.009$$
$$P(C \cap D) = 0.20 \times 0.05 = 0.010$$

Sum the probabilities using the law of total probability:
$$P(D) = 0.010 + 0.009 + 0.010 = 0.029$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
State the law of total probability across all three production sources:
$$P(D) = P(A)P(D \mid A) + P(B)P(D \mid B) + P(C)P(D \mid C)$$

Substitute numerical values for each route:
$$P(D) = (0.50 \times 0.02) + (0.30 \times 0.03) + (0.20 \times 0.05)$$

Evaluate the sum to obtain total defect rate:
$$P(D) = 0.010 + 0.009 + 0.010 = 0.029 = \frac{29}{1000}$$

ai_rubric.observable: State the law of total probability across all three machine routes: $P(D) = P(A)P(D \mid A) + P(B)P(D \mid B) + P(C)P(D \mid C)$.

parts.label: (b)
hints: Use Bayes' theorem: $P(B \mid D) = \frac{P(B \cap D)}{P(D)}$.
The numerator is Machine $B$'s defective rate: $0.30 \times 0.03 = 0.009$.
The denominator is the overall defective probability $0.029$ found in part (a).

walkthrough.text:
State the conditional probability formula:
$$P(B \mid D) = \frac{P(B \cap D)}{P(D)}$$

Substitute the values obtained in part (a):
$$P(B \cap D) = 0.009, \quad P(D) = 0.029$$

Simplify the fraction by eliminating decimals:
$$P(B \mid D) = \frac{0.009}{0.029} = \frac{9}{29}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Apply Bayes' theorem to find the posterior probability for Machine $B$:
$$P(B \mid D) = \frac{P(B \cap D)}{P(D)}$$

Insert the values determined from the tree paths in part (a):
$$P(B \mid D) = \frac{0.009}{0.029}$$

Simplify to an exact fraction in lowest terms:
$$P(B \mid D) = \frac{9}{29}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Substitute the numerator $0.30 \times 0.03 = 0.009$ and denominator $0.029$ from part (a).

parts.label: (a)
hints: Notice that the complement of 'at least one red' is 'no red marbles', meaning both selected marbles are white ($WW$).
Calculate $P(WW)$ without replacement: $\frac{4}{9} \times \frac{3}{8}$.
Subtract this complement probability from 1: $1 - P(WW)$.
Simplify your answer to an exact fraction.

walkthrough.text:
Determine the complement event of drawing zero red marbles:
$$P(\text{no red}) = P(WW) = \frac{4}{9} \times \frac{3}{8} = \frac{12}{72} = \frac{1}{6}$$

Apply the complement rule to find at least one red:
$$P(\ge 1 \text{ red}) = 1 - P(WW) = 1 - \frac{1}{6} = \frac{5}{6}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Formulate the complement probability of selecting two white marbles without replacement:
$$P(WW) = \frac{4}{9} \times \frac{3}{8} = \frac{12}{72} = \frac{1}{6}$$

Subtract the complement from 1 to obtain the required probability:
$$P(\ge 1 \text{ red}) = 1 - \frac{1}{6} = \frac{5}{6}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Use the complement rule $1 - P(WW)$ where $P(WW) = \frac{4}{9} \times \frac{3}{8}$ (or sum direct paths $RR + RW + WR$).

parts.label: (b)
hints: There are 5 red marbles out of 9 initially.
After one red marble is selected, 4 red marbles remain out of 8 total marbles.
Multiply along the path $(R_1, R_2)$ to find the joint probability.
Reduce the resulting fraction $\frac{20}{72}$ to lowest terms.

walkthrough.text:
State the probabilities of drawing red on the first and second draws without replacement:
$$P(R_1) = \frac{5}{9}, \quad P(R_2 \mid R_1) = \frac{4}{8}$$

Multiply along the path to obtain $P(RR)$:
$$P(RR) = \frac{5}{9} \times \frac{4}{8} = \frac{20}{72} = \frac{5}{18}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Update bag composition after the first red marble is taken:
$$\text{Draw 1: } \frac{5}{9}, \quad \text{Draw 2: } \frac{4}{8}$$

Multiply branch probabilities along the path:
$$P(RR) = \frac{5}{9} \times \frac{4}{8} = \frac{20}{72} = \frac{5}{18}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identify the sequential branch probabilities without replacement: $P(R_1) = \frac{5}{9}$ and $P(R_2 \mid R_1) = \frac{4}{8}$.

parts.label: (c)
hints: Use the conditional probability formula: $P(RR \mid \ge 1 R) = \frac{P(RR \cap (\ge 1 R))}{P(\ge 1 R)}$.
Because $RR$ is a subset of having at least one red, the numerator is simply $P(RR)$.
Substitute $P(RR) = \frac{5}{18}$ from part (b) and $P(\ge 1 R) = \frac{5}{6}$ from part (a).
Divide the two fractions and simplify completely.

walkthrough.text:
State the conditional probability relationship, noting that $RR \subseteq (\ge 1 R)$:
$$P(RR \mid \ge 1 R) = \frac{P(RR)}{P(\ge 1 R)}$$

Substitute the results from parts (a) and (b):
$$P(RR) = \frac{5}{18}, \quad P(\ge 1 R) = \frac{5}{6}$$

Divide and simplify the fraction:
$$P(RR \mid \ge 1 R) = \frac{5/18}{5/6} = \frac{5}{18} \times \frac{6}{5} = \frac{6}{18} = \frac{1}{3}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Recognize that the event 'both red' is completely contained within 'at least one red':
$$P(RR \mid \ge 1 R) = \frac{P(RR)}{P(\ge 1 R)}$$

Substitute the exact fractions calculated in parts (a) and (b):
$$\frac{P(RR)}{P(\ge 1 R)} = \frac{\frac{5}{18}}{\frac{5}{6}}$$

Cancel common factors to find the final reduced probability:
$$P = \frac{1}{3}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Formulate conditional probability: $P(RR \mid \ge 1 R) = \frac{P(RR)}{P(\ge 1 R)}$ noting that $RR \subseteq (\ge 1 R)$.
Substitute the numerator $\frac{5}{18}$ from part (b) and denominator $\frac{5}{6}$ from part (a).
Obtain correct simplified fraction $\frac{5/18}{5/6} = \frac{1}{3}$ (or recurring decimal $0.333$).

parts.label: (a)
hints: Drawing at least two red balls in 3 draws means either exactly 2 red balls or all 3 red balls.
List the 4 valid sequences: $RRR$, $RRN$, $RNR$, and $NRR$, where $N$ denotes non-red (green or blue, total 5 balls).
Compute the probability of $RRR$ and the probability of each 2-red arrangement without replacement.
Sum all 4 path probabilities to find the total.

walkthrough.text:
List the four mutually exclusive outcomes giving at least two red balls:
$$\text{Sequences} = \{RRR, RRN, RNR, NRR\}, \quad \text{where } N \in \{\text{Green}, \text{Blue}\}$$

Calculate probabilities along each path without replacement:
$$P(RRR) = \frac{4}{9} \times \frac{3}{8} \times \frac{2}{7} = \frac{24}{504} = \frac{1}{21} = \frac{2}{42}$$
$$P(RRN) = P(RNR) = P(NRR) = \frac{4}{9} \times \frac{3}{8} \times \frac{5}{7} = \frac{60}{504} = \frac{5}{42}$$

Sum the probabilities of all valid paths:
$$P(\ge 2 \text{ red}) = \frac{2}{42} + 3 \times \frac{5}{42} = \frac{2 + 15}{42} = \frac{17}{42}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Partition the event 'at least 2 red' into all 3 red and exactly 2 red:
$$P(\ge 2 R) = P(RRR) + 3 \times P(2R, 1N)$$

Calculate probabilities along paths without replacement:
$$P(RRR) = \frac{4 \times 3 \times 2}{9 \times 8 \times 7} = \frac{24}{504} = \frac{2}{42}, \quad P(2R, 1N) = \frac{4 \times 3 \times 5}{9 \times 8 \times 7} = \frac{60}{504} = \frac{5}{42}$$

Sum to obtain the total probability:
$$P(\ge 2 R) = \frac{2}{42} + \frac{15}{42} = \frac{17}{42}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identify the four mutually exclusive outcomes with at least two red balls without replacement: $RRR$ and the 3 permutations of 2 red and 1 non-red ($RRN, RNR, NRR$).

parts.label: (b)
hints: Use conditional probability: $P(\text{all } 3 \text{ red} \mid \ge 2 \text{ red}) = \frac{P(RRR)}{P(\ge 2 \text{ red})}$.
Notice that all 3 red is already one of the cases included in the denominator.
Substitute the numerator $P(RRR) = \frac{1}{21} = \frac{2}{42}$ and the denominator $\frac{17}{42}$ from part (a).
Simplify the fraction to lowest terms.

walkthrough.text:
Set up the conditional probability ratio:
$$P(RRR \mid \ge 2 R) = \frac{P(RRR \cap (\ge 2 R))}{P(\ge 2 R)} = \frac{P(RRR)}{P(\ge 2 R)}$$

Substitute the exact fractions calculated in part (a):
$$P(RRR) = \frac{2}{42}, \quad P(\ge 2 R) = \frac{17}{42}$$

Cancel the common denominator 42:
$$P(RRR \mid \ge 2 R) = \frac{2/42}{17/42} = \frac{2}{17}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Apply conditional probability within the restricted sample space:
$$P(\text{all } 3 R \mid \ge 2 R) = \frac{P(RRR)}{P(\ge 2 R)}$$

Insert the calculated probabilities from part (a):
